subject: Operational proof for 'no-model-learning' commitment and prompt/response IP
messages:
From: Jessica Barnes <jessica@healthbridge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@healthbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2024 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Operational evidence request - no-model-learning + IP and transfers

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team needs concrete operational evidence that HealthBridge data will not be used to improve models (we'll refer to this as a hard 'no-model-learning' commitment). Specifically they asked for:

- A short ops runbook describing how requests containing customer prompts are handled end-to-end (from ingestion -> KV/cache -> ephemeral storage -> deletion).
- A current list of subprocessors and whether any have access to raw prompts or KV caches.
- How prompt/response ownership is recorded (audit trail) and where output IP rights are documented.
- Cross-border transfer controls (are any subprocessors outside the US? any transfers to EU/APAC? onshore KMS?).
- Example artifacts: a sanitized audit log extract or an exported telemetry snippet showing retention TTLs and deletion timestamps.

Can you provide a one-page operational summary and a small set of artifacts we can include in our DPA exhibit? We don't need full logs — just sample lines and a diagram plus the runbook would help.

Regards,
Jessica
Procurement, HealthBridge

---
Attachment: requirements_matrix.xlsx (summary list)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Barnes <jessica@healthbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2024 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational evidence request - no-model-learning + IP and transfers

Hi Jessica — thanks, and great to meet on the call. Short answer: we can provide the artifacts you listed. Below is an operational summary and a plan for the deliverables.

Operational summary (high level):
- Ingestion: Customer requests land on a dedicated regional ingress fleet. Prompts are routed to a per-tenant ephemeral processing path. No writes are made to long-term model training stores.
- KV and cache: KV cache is in-memory per-session; persisted only to ephemeral local SSDs with an automated zeroize TTL (default 24h for enterprise customers; can be set to 0 for HealthBridge).
- Logging/audit trail: We emit structured telemetry (request id, tenant id, model id, route, retention TTL, deletion mark). Raw prompt text can be redacted from audit exports; we can provide a sanitized sample.
- Subprocessors: We maintain an inventory; subprocessors with potential access to plain-text prompts are: (1) on-prem consultant (no access by default), (2) managed infra provider (US-only, SOC 2) used for backup snapshots — backups exclude prompt text; (3) telemetry vendor (ingests metrics only).
- Transfers & KMS: Customer data at rest is optionally encrypted with onshore KMS. Cross-border transfers are controlled via route policies; by default HealthBridge traffic can be pinned to US-only.
- IP & ownership: Our DPA appendix states that customer-provided prompts and model outputs are customer content; Redwood will not assert ownership over prompt/response content. We keep an auditable record of output delivery (request id + artifact hashes).

Planned deliverables (ETA in business days):
1) One-page runbook (PDF) describing the steps above + operational controls. (OLGA: 2 business days)
2) Subprocessor inventory export (CSV) with access notes. (DAVID: 3 business days)
3) Sanitized audit sample (redacted lines showing TTL and deletion marks). (KARTHIK: 2 business days)
4) Dataflow diagram showing KMS & onshore routing. (OLGA: 2 business days)

We will attach the runbook and a short diagram in our next reply. Let me know if HealthBridge needs narrower retention (we can set TTL=0) or additional contractual language around the no-learning commitment.

Best,
Olga
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none in this message

From: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@healthbridge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Jessica Barnes <jessica@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2024 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational evidence request - no-model-learning + IP and transfers

Olga / team — quick follow-up from legal:

1) The subprocessor inventory should indicate whether subprocessors can access prompt text at-rest or in-flight. Please flag any third parties that have potential live access for debugging or emergency access.
2) For transfers: if any backups or monitoring pipelines ever replicate data to non-US locations, we need the exact controls and any contractual safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses, binding corporate rules, or onshore-only clauses).
3) For IP: can you give a short example of the audit record for output delivery (we do not need the actual output, just metadata and persistence path).

Also — we may ask for an evidence call (30 minutes) where your infra/ops engineer can walk our security folks through the runbook. Can you indicate who from Redwood can join?

Thanks,
Adeel
Counsel, HealthBridge

Attachment: legal_asks.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@healthbridge.com>, Jessica Barnes <jessica@healthbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Nov 2024 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational evidence request - no-model-learning + IP and transfers

Adeel / Jessica — attaching the initial artifact package per the plan.

What is attached (sanitized for DPA exhibit):
- no-learning-runbook_v1.pdf — 2 pages describing the operational flow, toggles to disable KV persistence, and the retention/deletion TTL controls.
- subprocessor-inventory_2024.csv — exported inventory with a redaction column; items marked "access: none" denote no access to raw prompt text.
- dataflow_onshore_kms.png — diagram showing regional routing and onshore KMS option.
- sanitized-audit-sample.txt — three lines showing request_id, tenant_id (hashed), retention_ttl, deletion_mark_timestamp.

Direct answers to your bullets:
- Subprocessors with potential live access are explicitly flagged in the CSV; we operate a US-only managed infra lane and can pin HealthBridge to that lane. No backups containing prompt text are replicated outside the US for that lane.
- We support SCCs / contractual assurances; we can add an onshore-only transfer clause to the DPA exhibit for HealthBridge.
- Example audit record (sample line in attached sanitized file):
  request_id=fb7a1d2c
  tenant_hash=e3b0c442
  model_id=gpt-redwood-22
  retention_ttl_s=0
  deletion_mark=2024-11-14T14:55:03Z

Ops participants for an evidence call: David Kim (Infra/ops) and Karthik Iyer (Security/controls). They're copied here and can do a 30-minute walkthrough early next week.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether the artifacts meet legal compliance needs; if so, we'll prepare a signed DPA exhibit and include the onshore-only clause.
- If you want a live demo of TTL zeroing and KV flush, we can schedule a sandbox session.

Best regards,
Olga
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: no-learning-runbook_v1.pdf, subprocessor-inventory_2024.csv, dataflow_onshore_kms.png, sanitized-audit-sample.txt
